messages:
morgan: @here seeing an increase in provisioning failures in eu-west-3 since the 03:00 BMC firmware rollout. ~14 nodes stuck in PXE stage, OOB consoles report "sol disconnected" intermittently.

sasha: are these the new 80gpu racks?

morgan: yes, 4 racks (rack-eu3-11..14). GPUs are healthy from OS side but our provisioner can't get IPMI SOL reliably.

lee: quick checks: ran `ipmitool -I lanplus -H 10.2.11.5 -U admin lan print` and seeing repeated "Session invalid" responses. Also saw ARP table storms on the oob switch port.

arun: @morgan can you paste journal logs from the provisioner for one failed node?

morgan: pasted snippets: `journalctl -u redwood-provisioner -n 200 | grep rack-eu3-12` ->
"May 03 03:12:11 provisioner[2245]: failed to claim node rack-eu3-12: sol: timeout"
"May 03 03:12:17 provisioner[2245]: ipmitool: Invalid Session ID"

devops-bot: deploy-bmc-fw.sh completed: rollout v1.4.8 -> v1.5.0 on rack-eu3-11..14 at 03:01 UTC (canary passed).

lee: interesting — canary passed but scale exposed this. Switch teams report occasional ARP flaps on the oob VLAN at the same time window. Might be a firmware change in the NIC controller on the BMC causing gratuitous ARP bursts.

sasha: this is blocking capacity. Customers with reserved capacity on eu-west-3 are getting scaled-down GPU allocations and we're incurring overflow costs on Dedicated. Need triage and mitigation.

arun: agreed. mitigation options: 1) roll back BMC FW on affected racks to v1.4.8, 2) isolate oob ports into separate VLANs to prevent ARP storms from affecting other racks, 3) add IPMI request rate-limiting in provisioner (short-term).

morgan: trying a rolling rollback on rack-eu3-12 now (tftp image). If rollback succeeds, we'll verify SOL and ipmitool sessions.

lee: if rollback fails, we need to run a low-level BMC reset sequence (clear NV ram + cold reset). I can prepare the runbook.

oncall-bot: @oncall morgan assigned (eu-west-3). Escalation policy: firmware-team if rollback + resets don't restore SOL in 30m.

morgan: update: rollback to v1.4.8 started on rack-eu3-12 at 03:28 UTC. SOL came back for 2 nodes, but 6 still flapping.

sasha: can someone capture `ethtool -S` on the BMC NIC when it's flapping? switch counters could mislead us.

lee: grabbing `ethtool -S ipmi0` now, sending output to #eng-infra-logs. snippet: "rx_errors: 0, tx_errors: 0, rx_packets: 123456, tx_packets: 123460, rx_arp: 9876, gratuitous_arp: 1248"

arun: gratuitous_arp spike is telling. We'll open a bug with the firmware team. In parallel: Sasha, can you approve expanding burst capacity for eu-west-3 for next 4 hours? We need to avoid SLA breaches while we fix.

sasha: approved. increasing burst pool + tagging affected customers. Finance — note likely extra spend, estimate +$7k for the day.

morgan: rolling rollback continuing across racks. If we see the gratuitous ARP metric drop after rollback, we'll plan a full fleet rollback and halt v1.5.0 rollout elsewhere.

devops-bot: rollback job scheduled: rollback-bmc-v1.5.0->1.4.8 on rack-eu3-11..14 in batches of 1 rack every 10m.

lee: FYI I'll add a temp iptables rule on the oob proxy to drop excessive ARP requests as a short-lived mitigation.

arun: filing internal incident: INC-2025-0667 with tags [bmc, oob, secureboot?]. Note: secure boot flags didn't flip, but boot order was jittery on two nodes — include in RCA scope.

morgan: thanks all — will post results in ~40m. :white_check_mark:
